meta.note: Static, rule-based preference quiz for the 'Find Your Path' feature — no AI/LLM involved, just fixed point values summed per role track. Question axes and point assignments are grounded in real precedent: CompTIA's own offensive-vs-defensive career framing, LetsDefend's SOC-vs-pentester comparison, the NICE Workforce Framework's Securely Provision / Protect & Defend / Analyze categories, and Coursera's/SANS's existing cybersecurity career quizzes (interest, activity preference, problem-solving mindset, work rhythm, learning style, motivation, entry-path pragmatism axes). Compiled via a Researcher web-search pass, 2026-08-01 — see AGENT_STATE.md for sourcing.
meta.scoring: Each selected option adds its listed points to one or more role tracks. Highest total wins; if the top two tracks are within 2 points of each other (or tie outright), the result falls back to Cybersecurity Intern/Generalist rather than guessing between two closely-matched tracks.

questions.prompt: When you hear about a security breach, what are you most curious about?

options.label: Investigating what happened and how to catch it next time
Figuring out exactly how the attacker got in
Whether the network/systems were built to prevent it in the first place
All of it equally — I want to learn the whole picture

questions.prompt: Which task sounds most appealing to spend a workday on?

options.label: Watching dashboards/alerts and triaging what looks suspicious
Trying creative ways to break into a test system
Configuring firewalls, VPNs, and network access rules
Not sure yet — I'd rather get exposure to a few of these first

questions.prompt: Which work rhythm appeals to you more?

options.label: Team-based, ongoing shift monitoring
Defined engagements with a clear start/end and a report to deliver
Long-term ownership of infrastructure that evolves over time
Open to any of these

questions.prompt: How do you prefer to solve problems?

options.label: Spotting patterns/anomalies in data over time
Finding the one unconventional way past a defense
Designing something resilient from the start
Depends entirely on the problem in front of me

questions.prompt: How do you like to learn technical skills?

options.label: Following structured playbooks/procedures
Experimenting and breaking things without a fixed process
Understanding how protocols/hardware/systems fit together
Still exploring — no strong preference yet

questions.prompt: What would feel like a genuine win to you?

options.label: Catching an intruder before real damage happens
Proving a system can be broken and clearly explaining how
Zero incidents because the architecture was airtight
Just getting my foot in the door anywhere in security

questions.prompt: Which entry path sounds most realistic for you right now?

options.label: A junior monitoring role I can grow from quickly
